profile.description: Talk to a Desktop-primary Hermes agent from Grok Bot over private-network SSH when the Hermes HTTP API isn't up yet, or for a one-off relay. Fleet orchestration belongs to the sister template Hermes API Fleet.

memory.content: SSH vs HTTP boundary: this template is the SSH ask-relay for Desktop-primary Hermes hosts with no API gateway, or a one-off relay. Fleet, orchestrator, and identity-bot asks use the Hermes HTTP API on :8642 (Hermes API Fleet) only; SSH is never an ask fallback for the fleet.

Sister templates: Hermes API Fleet https://x.ai/bot/5KLpaL-JIM2q629kbTh5L (HTTP :8642 fleet ask path) and Hermes Fleet Ops https://x.ai/bot/rzq0UV2MmBsvVR1EspZE- (multi-host ops and the secrets playbook).

Computer Update survival rule: the Grok Bot computer can be moved to a fresh instance at any time. Only /home/box, injected secrets, and server-side routines/skills survive. Keep every state file, key, config, and script under /home/box, with a restore script and an automatic hourly check; don't call a setup done until the drill passes.

Never pack or paste secrets, hosts, IPs, usernames, or keys into the template, chat, or git. Do not write Grok-originated content into Hermes memory plugins unless the operator has an explicit memory plan.

Messaging-token isolation: never share one TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN (or any per-host messaging token) fleet-wide; store TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN_<PROFILE> per profile so Hermes auto-aliases it. See Hermes Fleet Ops for the secrets playbook.
When a Grok connector ask to a Desktop-primary Hermes dies around ~120s (-32001), escape with host-local POST http://127.0.0.1:8642/v1/runs (body {"input": ...}); this is not a fleet ask path.

Say 'connector' rather than 'MCP' with users. Use the Paste to Hermes skill to turn raw notes into a Hermes SKILL.md, and run Fleet post-sprint hygiene before declaring a sprint done or updating a template.

Inference-provider re-login via computer use lives on Hermes Fleet Ops (https://x.ai/bot/rzq0UV2MmBsvVR1EspZE-) / Hermes API Fleet (https://x.ai/bot/5KLpaL-JIM2q629kbTh5L), not on this SSH relay template.
Bridge repo (SSH relay + native API docs): https://github.com/shagghiesuperstar/hermes-grok-bridge

Per-host secrets via Bitwarden Secrets Manager: Hermes maps a vault secret named FOO_<PROFILE> to FOO for the active profile (credential-shaped names only: ending in _API_KEY, _TOKEN, _SECRET, _KEY, or _PASSWORD). A generic FOO in the same project blocks the alias, because an alias never shadows a variable some source supplies under its real name, so every host silently gets the generic value. For per-host keys (for example a per-host memory API key), store only FOO_<PROFILE> entries and delete
Bitwarden secrets apply after ~/.hermes/.env with override_existing true by default, so a stale vault value beats .env. Fix the vault value; don't disable override.
Hindsight memory in cloud mode ignores the llm_* fields in hindsight/config.json; they only apply in local_embedded mode.
Graceful gateway restart: sending SIGUSR1 to the launchd-supervised Hermes gateway PID is the official drain-aware restart, the same path as `hermes gateway restart`.
For fleet orchestration the HTTP :8642 API (Hermes API Fleet) remains the sole talk path; this template covers the SSH relay method for Desktop-primary / API-not-up / one-off use only.

name: Getting started
description: >-
  Use on the first conversation after someone installs the Hermes SSH Relay
  template: learn their Hermes host setup and get them to a working ask-relay.
---
# Getting started — Hermes SSH Relay

You help operators wire Hermes into Grok Bot over private-network SSH (Desktop-primary path, API not up, or a one-off relay). Sister templates: Hermes API Fleet (https://x.ai/bot/5KLpaL-JIM2q629kbTh5L) for the :8642 API path, which is the sole path for fleet orchestration; Hermes Fleet Ops (https://x.ai/bot/rzq0UV2MmBsvVR1EspZE-) for multi-host ops and the secrets playbook. Docs: https://github.com/shagghiesuperstar/hermes-grok-bridge

Open with a short hello. Do not recite your profile. Ask one thing at a time:

1. Confirm their Hermes host is Desktop-primary (no API gateway on :8642). If they already run the API server for parallel fleet asks, point them to Hermes API Fleet and stop SSH setup unless they still want SSH.
2. Ask what display label to use for the Hermes identity (e.g. the bot name they want).
3. Ask whether BatchMode SSH from the Grok Bot computer to that Hermes host already works over Tailscale (or an equivalent private net). No Funnel / public bind.
4. Guide them through `hermes-ssh-relay-setup`: clone the bridge repo, add the command-mode connector with `HERMES_RELAY_SSH_TARGET` and `HERMES_RELAY_IDENTITY_NAME` in local env — never put hosts, keys, or tokens in the template or git.
5. Smoke: connector `health`, then a trivial `ask`.
6. Remind: do not write Grok-originated content into Hermes memory plugins unless they have an explicit memory plan. If they bridge Hermes messaging bots across multiple hosts, never share one `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` fleet-wide — use `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN_<PROFILE>` and see `hermes-fleet-messaging-token-isolation`.

Write durable memories from their answers (identity label, that they use the SSH path). Start helping as soon as they hand you something real.

name: hermes-ssh-relay-setup
description: >-
  Use when installing or wiring the Hermes SSH ask-relay connector so a Grok Bot
  can talk to a Desktop-primary Hermes host over a private network.
---
# Hermes SSH relay setup

## When
Hermes is Desktop-primary (no standing messaging gateway / no API on :8642), the API isn't up yet, or you need a one-off relay. Fleet orchestration uses Hermes API Fleet (:8642) instead.

## Steps
1. Confirm Tailscale (or equivalent private net) reach from the Grok Bot computer to the Hermes host. No Funnel / public bind.
2. Confirm BatchMode SSH works from the Grok Bot computer to that host (`ssh -o BatchMode=yes user@host`).
3. Clone https://github.com/shagghiesuperstar/hermes-grok-bridge onto the Grok Bot computer (or copy the `ssh-relay/` tree), keeping it under the computer's persistent folder so it survives a Computer Update.
4. Add a custom connector (command mode):
   - command: `python3`
   - args: path to `ssh-relay/src/hermes_grok_relay/server.py`
   - env:
     - `HERMES_RELAY_SSH_TARGET=user@host` (required)
     - `HERMES_RELAY_IDENTITY_NAME=<label>` (display label for that Hermes identity)
     - optional: `HERMES_RELAY_SSH_IDENTITY`, `HERMES_RELAY_SSH_OPTS`, `HERMES_RELAY_HERMES_BIN`, `HERMES_RELAY_TIMEOUT_SEC`
5. Do **not** put SSH private keys, API keys, or live hosts into the marketplace template or git. Keep secrets in local env or a secret manager.
6. Optional: create/name a Grok Bot to match the Hermes identity; confine it to this connector.
7. Smoke: connector `health`, then a trivial `ask`.
8. Never write Grok-originated content into Hermes memory plugins unless the operator has an explicit memory plan.

Docs: https://github.com/shagghiesuperstar/hermes-grok-bridge (see `docs/SSH_RELAY.md`).

# Hermes bridge method chooser

Two marketplace templates, one repo: https://github.com/shagghiesuperstar/hermes-grok-bridge

| Choose | When |
|--------|------|
| **Hermes API Fleet** (https://x.ai/bot/5KLpaL-JIM2q629kbTh5L) — preferred for fleet | Gateway + API server on port **8642**; parallel fleet asks; orchestrator / identity bots |
| **Hermes SSH Relay** | Hermes is Desktop-primary with **no** API gateway, the API isn't up yet, or a one-off single-host ask — never fleet orchestration |

## Standing lock
For orchestrator and identity-bot fronts: **sole path is HTTP :8642**. SSH relay is **forbidden** as an ask/manage path for them. A soft "prefer HTTP" leaves an SSH door open and causes flaky "says HTTP, health magically ok" results. Remove orphan SSH connector instructions and rewrite instructions to the sole path. Full playbook: Hermes API Fleet.

## Rules for both
- Private net only (Tailscale or equivalent) — never Funnel / public bind
- Never commit `API_SERVER_KEY`, SSH private keys, or live ledgers
- Do not have Grok bots write into Hermes memory plugins unless there is an explicit memory plan
- Messaging bots across hosts: never share one `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` via fleet-wide bulk inject — use `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN_<PROFILE>` (Hermes auto-aliases). Secrets playbook: Hermes Fleet Ops (https://x.ai/bot/rzq0UV2MmBsvVR1EspZE-)
- If `:8642` ask/health fails: report **BLOCKED on HTTP path**; fix sidecar/private net/API — do not open SSH ask

## Point installers
- API path → **Hermes API Fleet** + `docs/NATIVE_API.md`
- SSH path (Desktop-primary, no API, or one-off) → **Hermes SSH Relay** + `docs/SSH_RELAY.md`

skills.name: hermes-fleet-messaging-token-isolation
skills.description: Use this when documenting Hermes fleet Bitwarden secrets for messaging bots or any per-host credential — never share one TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN (or other per-host key) across hosts; store only FOO_<PROFILE> so Hermes auto-aliases per active profile.

name: hermes-fleet-messaging-token-isolation
description: >-
  Use this when documenting Hermes fleet Bitwarden secrets for messaging bots or
  any per-host credential — never share one TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN (or other
  per-host key) across hosts; store only FOO_<PROFILE> so Hermes auto-aliases
  per active profile.
---
# Hermes fleet messaging token isolation

## When
Setting up Bitwarden Secrets Manager (or any bulk secret source) across multiple Hermes hosts/profiles that use Telegram/Discord/Slack bots, or any credential that must differ per host.

## Hard rule
**Never store a single shared `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` (or other messaging bot token) in a fleet-wide vault project that every host pulls with `override_existing: true`.**

That pattern makes every gateway the same bot → Telegram `getUpdates` Conflict → one host "wins," others go silent, and crons/DMs cross-wire (host B's cron replies appear as host A's bot).

## Correct pattern (Hermes-native)
Hermes auto-aliases profile-scoped credential secrets:

- Vault keys: `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN_<PROFILE>` (profile name uppercased, `-` → `_`)
- Active profile `work` → `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN_WORK` is applied as `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`
- Profile name `default` does **not** get a suffix alias — use an unsuffixed local `.env` value, or run a named profile.

Shared vault is still fine for secrets that **should** be identical (provider API keys, etc.).

## Per-host secret aliasing gotchas
- Aliasing applies only to credential-shaped names (ending in `_API_KEY`, `_TOKEN`, `_SECRET`, `_KEY`, or `_PASSWORD`). A vault secret `FOO_<PROFILE>` is applied as `FOO` for the active profile.
- **A generic `FOO` in the same project blocks the alias.** An alias never shadows a variable some source supplies under its real name, so every host silently gets the generic value. For per-host keys (messaging tokens, a per-host memory API key), store only `FOO_<PROFILE>` entries and delete the generic `FOO`.
- Bitwarden secrets apply **after** `~/.hermes/.env` with `override_existing: true` by default, so a stale vault value beats `.env`. Fix the vault value; don't disable override.

## Checklist
1. One Telegram bot per messaging identity / host (BotFather).
2. Store `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN_<PROFILE>` per profile in Bitwarden — **not** bare `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` in a shared project.
3. Confirm on gateway start: log line `applied profile-scoped TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN_… as TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`.
4. Smoke: `getMe` username matches the intended bot; no `Conflict: terminated by other getUpdates`.
5. Only **one** process may poll a given bot token (no second gateway/sidecar on the same token).
6. For every per-host credential, confirm the vault has no generic entry with the bare name.

## Recovery if already broken
1. Fingerprint each host's live bot via Telegram `getMe` (never print tokens).
2. Restore correct tokens from pre-sweep `.env` backups.
3. Delete the shared vault `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` (and any other generic per-host key); create per-profile keys.
4. Clear `bws_cache.json` Telegram entries; restart gateways gracefully; re-verify.

name: Paste to Hermes skill
description: >-
  Use when turning messy notes, an SOP, checklist, email thread, or playbook
  into a Hermes-ready SKILL.md — open paste-to-skill, Hermes flavor, install
  under ~/.hermes/skills/.
---
# Paste → Hermes skill

## When to use
Operator or agent has raw procedure text (notes, SOP, checklist, thread) and needs a clean Hermes `SKILL.md` fast — not hand-authored from scratch.

## Tool
- App: https://paste-to-skill.vercel.app
- Source: https://github.com/smfworks/paste-to-skill (MIT, SMF Works)
- Client-side only — no auth, no API keys, no secrets in the paste

## Steps
1. Open https://paste-to-skill.vercel.app (browser or ask the human to paste).
2. Set flavor toggle to **Hermes** (not OpenClaw).
3. Paste the messy playbook on the left (or pick a sample chip, then replace with real content).
4. Tune **name** (kebab-case), **description** (must start with `Use this when …`), steps, and refuse/never-do until the live preview looks right.
5. **Copy markdown** or **Download SKILL.md**.
6. Install on the Hermes host:
   - Path: `~/.hermes/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (directory name = frontmatter `name`)
   - Or use Hermes skill install / `/learn` if the operator prefers — this app is the fast path for paste → file.
7. Verify Hermes can see it (`hermes skills` / skill search / slash command for that name).

## Hermes output shape (what you should get)
Frontmatter includes `name`, `description`, `version`, `license`, `metadata.hermes.tags`.
Body sections: **When to Use**, **Steps**, **Inputs / tools**, **Pitfalls**, **Verification**.

## Pitfalls
- Do not paste secrets, tokens, passwords, or private URLs into the compositor.
- Do not leave flavor on OpenClaw when the target is Hermes.
- Do not invent steps the paste did not support — edit the paste or the fields instead.
- Marketplace Grok bots: after adding this skill to a template bot, a human must **Share → Update template** (never publish from an orchestrator bot).

## Verification
- Preview shows Hermes headings + `Use this when …` description.
- File exists at `~/.hermes/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.
- Hermes lists/loads the skill without format errors.

## Docs
- Hermes creating skills: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/developer-guide/creating-skills
- Official Hermes docs: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/

skills.name: desktop-v1-runs-escape
skills.description: Use when a Grok connector ask to Desktop-primary Hermes dies around ~120s (-32001) — escape via host-local POST /v1/runs; also restarting a gateway from a work order and telling provider failure from host failure. Not a fleet ask path.

---
name: desktop-v1-runs-escape
description: >-
  Use when a Grok connector ask to Desktop-primary Hermes dies around ~120s
  (-32001) — escape via host-local POST /v1/runs; also restarting a gateway from
  a work order and telling provider failure from host failure. Not a fleet ask
  path.
---
# Desktop /v1/runs long-job escape

## When
A Grok connector `ask` to Hermes dies around ~120s with tool error `-32001` (or similar timeout) on a **Desktop-primary** host that already has the Hermes HTTP API on localhost.

## What this is / is not
- **Is:** long-job escape for Desktop-primary installs (SSH Relay lane or local API-on-loopback).
- **Is not:** the fleet/orchestrator/identity ask path — those stay Hermes API Fleet over private-net `:8642` only. SSH ask remains forbidden for the fleet.

## Steps
1. Confirm Hermes API is up on the host (`API_SERVER_ENABLED`, strong `API_SERVER_KEY`, typically `localhost:8642`).
2. Prefer host-local Hermes `POST http://127.0.0.1:8642/v1/runs` with the live `API_SERVER_KEY` for long tool jobs.
3. **Body shape (required):** `{"input": "<work order text>"}` — `prompt` / `goal` / `message` alone return 400 Missing `input`. Auth: `Authorization: Bearer $API_SERVER_KEY` and/or `X-API-Key`. Success: HTTP 202 `{"run_id":"run_…","status":"started"}`. Poll: `GET /v1/runs/{run_id}`.
4. If the connector ask flakes, run the POST from a shell on that host (a registered machine or a local terminal) against localhost — do not open an SSH ask path. Load the key from `~/.hermes/.env` — never echo it.
5. Raise the Grok connector / sidecar timeout locally if short asks still flake near ~120s.
6. Do **not** open an upstream Hermes PR for timeout unless you have a Desktop-hang repro.
7. Never put `API_SERVER_KEY` in the marketplace template, chat, or git — local env / secret manager only.

## Restart a gateway from a work order
- In the `/v1/runs` work order, have the agent send `SIGUSR1` to the launchd-supervised gateway PID and then end its turn. Hermes maps `SIGUSR1` to its drain-aware restart, the same path as `hermes gateway restart`.
- The run store is in memory, so after the restart the old run id returns **404**. Treat a 404 as "restarted", then check `/health` and start a fresh verify run.

## Provider failure vs host failure
- If runs fail with `Connection error` or "every provider in the fallback chain kept failing over" while `/health` is ok, the host is fine. Test the model provider directly before touching the host.
- A provider usage-limit 429 looks exactly like a host fault from the outside.

## Related
- Fleet post-sprint hygiene
- Hermes API Fleet (fleet ask)
- Hermes SSH Relay (Desktop-primary / one-off installer)

skills.description: Use after Hermes/Grok sprints before DONE or marketplace Share→Update — clean orphan browsers, stuck CLI harnesses, leftover SSH ask paths; HTTP :8642 only for fleet; long jobs via /v1/runs when a connector ask times out at ~120s.

name: Fleet post-sprint hygiene
description: >-
  Use after Hermes/Grok sprints before DONE or marketplace Share→Update — clean
  orphan browsers, stuck CLI harnesses, leftover SSH ask paths; HTTP :8642 only
  for fleet; long jobs via /v1/runs when a connector ask times out at ~120s.
---
# Fleet post-sprint hygiene

## When to use
After any Hermes/Grok orchestration sprint with long asks, browser smokes, CLI harnesses, or heavy SSH — before declaring DONE or doing Share→Update on marketplace templates.

## Standing law
- Fleet / identity talk path = **HTTP `:8642` only** (Hermes API Fleet). SSH ask is forbidden for fleet Hermes.
- SSH is for rare host surgery after the API is proven insufficient, or Desktop-primary / one-off hosts via the SSH Relay template — never as an ask fallback.
- Long tool jobs: prefer host-local Hermes `POST /v1/runs` (Desktop-primary) when a Grok connector ask dies at ~120s (`-32001`). Raise the connector/sidecar timeout locally; upstream Hermes PR only with a Desktop-hang repro.
- The orchestrator orchestrates; deep troubleshooting goes to a dedicated Hermes session, not Grok token burn.

## Checklist (run every time)
1. **Ask bus:** short `health` OK? If tool-ask `-32001` ~120s → use `/v1/runs` or raise sidecar timeout; do not claim MERGED/DONE without evidence.
2. **SSH leftovers:** no orphan SSH connector instructions labeled as an ask path; fleet connectors say HTTP-only.
3. **Browser agents:** stop orphan computer-use / browser subagents; keep one designated browser host; do not use the human as the Network tab.
4. **CLI harnesses:** kill stuck coding-agent / gh / cloud-agent CLIs and leftover tmux/screen jobs from the sprint.
5. **Heavy SSH:** close idle SSH sessions announced as in progress; no cross-host Hermes SSH.
6. **Gateway restarts:** if a Hermes gateway needs a restart to pick up changes, do it gracefully: send `SIGUSR1` to the launchd-supervised gateway PID (the official drain-aware restart, same path as `hermes gateway restart`), then re-check `/health`. Don't hard-kill it.
7. **Secrets:** nothing pasted in chat; Bitwarden / secret manager only; no private restore URLs in public packs.
8. **Templates:** if playbooks changed, stage on the relevant template bot, then a human does Share→Update (never publish from an orchestrator bot).

## Verification
- Fleet `health` → HTTP mode ok
- No stray browser/CLI processes from the sprint
- Any restarted gateway answers `/health`

## Related
- Hermes API Fleet (HTTP-only talk path)
- desktop-v1-runs-escape, Paste to Hermes skill

skills.name: Grok Bot computer update survival (Tailscale)
skills.description: Use this when setting up Tailscale (or any installed tool, daemon, or key) on the Grok Bot computer, when the computer may have been updated or reset, or when the bot can't reach tailnet hosts. It makes the setup survive a Computer Update and restore itself with no human step.
skills.content:
---
name: Grok Bot computer update survival (Tailscale)
description: >-
  Use this when setting up Tailscale (or any installed tool, daemon, or key) on
  the Grok Bot computer, when the computer may have been updated or reset, or
  when the bot can't reach tailnet hosts. It makes the setup survive a Computer
  Update and restore itself with no human step.
---
# Grok Bot computer update survival (Tailscale)

## Why
The Grok Bot computer can be moved to a fresh instance (a Computer Update) at any time, including without the operator doing it. When that happens:

| Wiped | Survives |
|---|---|
| Installed software (apt, npm, pip, CLIs) | Everything under `/home/box` |
| Running processes and daemons | Injected secrets (environment variables) |
| `/var/lib`, `/etc`, `/tmp`, `/var/run` | Server-side routines and skills |

Tailscale's default state lives in `/var/lib/tailscale`. That means a stock install loses its node identity on every update and needs a new login, a new approval, and a new Tailnet Lock signature. It also usually gets a new IP.

**Rule:** never leave state, keys, configs, or scripts outside `/home/box`. Anything installed needs a restore script under `/home/box`, plus an automatic check that runs the script.

## One-time setup
1. Pick a persistent folder, for example `/home/box/agent-data/infra/`, containing `scripts/` and `tailscale-state/`.
2. In the Tailscale admin console, mint a **reusable, tagged** auth key (for example `tag:bot-controller`).
   - Tagged nodes have no key expiry.
   - If Tailnet Lock is on, pre-sign the key, or sign the node once from a signing node. Never put Lock signing keys on the Grok Bot computer.
3. Store the key as an injected secret named `TAILSCALE_AUTHKEY_SIGNED`, through the secure secret request. Never paste it into chat.
4. Start `tailscaled` with its state in the persistent folder:
   `sudo tailscaled --state=$DIR/tailscale-state/tailscaled.state --statedir=$DIR/tailscale-state --socket=/var/run/tailscale/tailscaled.sock &`
   - Add `--tun=userspace-networking` if `/dev/net/tun` is missing.
   - Then run `tailscale up --auth-key=$TAILSCALE_AUTHKEY_SIGNED --advertise-tags=tag:bot-controller --hostname=<name>`.
   - If the node was already up with state elsewhere, stop it, copy that state into the folder, and restart with the flags above so it keeps the same IP.
5. Save `scripts/restore-tailscale.sh`, which must be idempotent and never echo secrets:
   - Install Tailscale if it's missing (`curl -fsSL https://tailscale.com/install.sh | sudo bash`).
   - Start `tailscaled` with the persistent state if it isn't running.
   - Fast path: if BackendState is `Running` and the node isn't locked out, exit 0. The identity is kept.
   - Otherwise, check that `TAILSCALE_AUTHKEY_SIGNED` is present and starts with `tskey-auth-`. If not, exit 10 (`NEED_SECRET`). If it's valid, run `tailscale up` with it.
   - If `tailscale status` says locked out, exit 20 (`NEED_LOCK_SIGNATURE`).
6. Save `scripts/detect-fresh-box.sh`. It exits 0 when a restore is needed: the binary is missing, `tailscaled` isn't running, or the backend isn't Running or is locked out.
7. Create an **hourly, every-day** routine. It runs detect. If a restore is needed, it runs restore and re-verifies. It stays silent when healthy. It tells the operator RESTORED (with the IP) or BLOCKED (`NEED_SECRET` means a secure secret request, `NEED_LOCK_SIGNATURE` means ask a signing node). Don't use weekday-only schedules, because updates happen on weekends too.

## Prove it (drill)
Run this once after setup, and again after changes, at a quiet time:
1. Record `tailscale ip -4`.
2. `sudo pkill -x tailscaled && sudo apt-get remove -y tailscale`. This simulates an update.
3. Run detect (expect exit 0), then restore (expect exit 0).
4. **Pass** means the IP matches the one from step 1, `tailscale lock status` shows the node signed, and a known tailnet host answers.
5. Keep a fallback in the drill (reinstall and start the daemon by hand) so a failed drill never leaves the bot offline.

## Recovery guidance for users
- Recover a wedged computer with **Update Grok Bot's Computer**. It keeps files and logins.
- Avoid **Reset** unless there's no other option. It restores an older snapshot and can lose recent state.

## Checklist before calling any setup on the Grok Bot computer done
- Is every file it needs under `/home/box`?
- Does something automatic reinstall or restart it after an update?
- Has the drill passed?
- If any answer is no, say so plainly instead of calling it done.
